senses.gloss:
अ॑न्न n. food, esp. boiled rice;
 p. ˚वन्त्.
1 अनग्नि॑ m. non-fire, anything else than fire.

अनङ्ग॑ a. bodiless;
 m. the god of love.

अनङ्गरति f. joy of love;
 a woman's name.

अनडुह m. (—˚) = seq. m.;
 f. ई॑ cow.
अ॑नणु a. not minute or small.

अनतिकृच्छ्रेण (instr. adv.) without too much pain
or trouble.
अ॑नतिक्रम m. अनतिक्रम˚ण† n. not overstepping.

अनतिक्रमणीय a. not to be overstepped or
transgressed, inviolable.
अनतिक्रुद्ध a. not too angry with (gen.).
अनतिपात्य a. not to be transgressed or neglected.

अनतिप्रकाशक n. not very enlightening (ph.);
abstr. ˚त्व n.

अनतिलम्बिन् a. not too much hanging or undulating,
rather tight (garment).

अनतिलुलित a. not too much pressed, not too closely
adhered to.
अ॑नद्धा adv. not truly or really.

अनद्यतन m. not this day, not to-day or the same day.
— भूतान˚ & भविष्यदन˚ not the same day in the past or in the
future.
अनध्यात्मविद् a. not knowing the supreme soul.
अननुरूप a. not fit, ill suited.

अनन्त॑ a. endless;
 m. Viṣṇu, a man's name.

अनन्तर॑ a. having nothing within or between,
immediately adjoining^1 or following (in time and space), next, esp. in
caste. अनन्तरम् adv. close by;
 thereupon, at once, soon after (gen.,
abl., or —˚).
[1] Correction submitted by AnnaRybakovaT, Jim Funderburk. Reference: https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/25.
अनन्तरज a. next born, also = seq.

अनन्तरजात a. born of a woman of lower caste than
the man's.

अनन्तविजय m. N. of Yudhiṣṭhira's conch-shell
(lit. counting endless victories).

आ॑नन्त्य a. infinite;
 n. infinity, immortality.
अनन्द m. pl. N. of a cert. world.

अनन्यचित्त a. having no other thought, quite
absorbed in (loc.).

अनन्य˚चेतस् a. having no other thought, quite
absorbed in (loc.).

अनन्यजन्मन् m. E. of the god of love (lit. born from
no other).

अनन्यदृष्टि a. having no other sight, looking at
nothing else.
अनन्यमनस् a. thinking of no other person or thing.

अनन्य˚मानस a. thinking of no other person or
thing.
अनन्यरुचि a. having no other desire.
अनन्यविषय a. relating to nothing else.
अनन्यसम a. having no equal unparalleled.
अनन्य˚सामान्य a. having no equal unparalleled.

अनन्यसाधारण f. ई a. belonging to (lit.
common with) no other.
अ॑नपराद्ध a. faultless, having done no harm.
अनपसर a. having no escape or excuse.

अनपेक्ष a. inconsiderate, careless;
 n. adv.
अनप्न॑स् a. having no possession, poor.

अनभिज्ञ a. unacquainted with, ignorant of (gen., loc.,
or —˚).

अनभिभवगन्ध a. showing no (smell of)
contempt.

अनभिसंधाय ger. having made no agreement;
taking no interest in anything.
अनभ्यर्थनीय a. not to be desired.*

अनमित्र॑ a. free from enemies;
 n. as abstr.
अनमित्रलाभ m. the not-getting of enemies.

अनमीव॑ a. having or causing no sickness or pain,
healthy, propitious. n. health, weal.

अनर्घ m. wrong (lit. no) value;
 a. priceless.
अनर्घराघव n. T. of a drama.

अनर्चित a. unpraised, unrespected, given without
respect.

अनर्थ a. useless, fruitless, unhappy, unlucky,
meaningless, nonsensical (also ˚क);
 m. non-advantage, disadvantage,
damage, ill-luck, nonsense.

अनर्थपण्डित a. learned or versed in useless
things.
अनर्थान्तर n. not another i.e. the same meaning.
अनर्थ्य॑ a. useless, good for nothing.
अनल m. fire or the god of fire.
अ॑नवकॢप्त a. irregular, wrong, unfit for (loc.).
अ॑नवगत a. not attained or understood.

अनवच्छिन्न a. undiscerned, undefined, indistinct;
abstr. ˚त्व n.
अनवद्याङ्ग f. ई having a faultless body.

अनवधान a. inattentive, careless;
 n. abstr.

अनवम a. not the lowest;
 —˚ = seq.

अनवरत a. uninterrupted, continual;
 n. adv.

अनवलेप a. not anointed or not haughty;
 m. modesty.

अनवसित a. = अनवस॑;
 f. आ N. of a metre.

अनवस्था f. instability, unboundedness, regressus in
infinitum (ph.).

अनवस्थित a. unsteady, fickle;
 abstr. ˚स्थिति f.

अनवाप्य a. not to be obtained;
 n. imp.

अनवेक्षण n. ˚क्षा f. want of attention,
regardlessness.

अनसूयक (f. अनसू˚यिका), अन˚सूयन्त्, & अन˚सूयु =
अनसूय a.

अनस्थि a. the same;
 s. a boneless animal.

अनहंवादिन् a. not talking (only) of one's self,
modest.
अ॑नागत a. not yet come, future.

अनागतविधातृ m. Disposer of the future (N. of a
fish).
अनाचरन्त् a. not doing or exercising.
अनातुर॑ a. not ill, well, healthy.
अनात्मज्ञ a. stupid (lit. not knowing one's self).
अनात्मत्व n. not being the soul.
1 अनाथ a. having no protector, helpless.
अनाद्य॑ a. uneatable, unfit for food.
अनापद् f. absence of calamity, misfortune, or need.
अ॑नापि a. having no friends or relations.

अ॑नाप्त a. not reaching or reached, not obtained or
obtainable, unskilful, unapt.
अनाप्ति f. non-obtaining, want of success, disappointment.
अनामयप्रश्न m. inquiry after one's health.
अनामुक्त a. not yet put on or worn.
अनायक a. without a leader or protector.

अ॑नायत a. not fastened;
 not long, short.

अनायतार्गल a. having its bolt not fastened,
unlocked (a house).

अनायास a. exempt from pain or difficulty, easy;
 m. abstr.
अनायुध॑ a. not having implements or weapons.
अनायुष्य a. not imparting i.e. shortening life.
अनारभ्य a. not to be undertaken, impossible.

अनार्य a. not-Aryan, un-Aryan, dishonourable, unworthy;
abstr. ˚ता f.
अनार्यकर्मिन् a. not acting like an Aryan.
अनार्ष a. not coming from or relating to a Ṛṣi.
अ॑नार्षेय a. not coming from or relating to a Ṛṣi.
अनाविल a. not turbid, clear, pure.

अनाविष्कृतपाप a. whose sins have not been made
known.
अनाश्रित a. not resorting to or caring for (acc.).

अनास्वादित a. not tasted;
 ˚पूर्व never before tasted.
अ॑नाहिताग्नि a. not having set up the sacred fire.
अन्नदोष m. fault committed by eating forbidden food.
अ॑न्नपति m. lord of food (E. of sev. gods).
अन्नपान n. pl. food and drink.

अन्नप्राशन n. (first) feeding (of an infant) with
rice ((r.)).
अन्नरस (n. sgl. & m. pl.) food and drink.
अन्नरसमय a. consisting of food and drink.

अन्नविकार m. transformation of food;
 abstr. ˚त्व.
अन्नशेष m. leavings of food, offal.
अन्नाद्यज a. born or bred in food.
आनक m. a kind of drum.

आनतपर्वन् a. having the knots or joints flatted;
smooth, polished (arrow).
आननचर f. ई falling into the mouth of (gen.).

आनन्तर्य n. absence of interval, immediate consequence
or succession.

आनन्दमय f. ई made up of joy, blissful. Abstr.
˚त्व n.
आनयन n. bringing towards, back, or about.
